Commentary.Commentary: All set for action. The Pakistani players are out in the middle. Mikyle Louis and Kraigg Brathwaite to open for West Indies. Sajid Khan has the new cherry in hand.

20 wickets on Day 1 has started this match at a rapid pace. Once again all the batters struggled but it was the Windies tail that made a massive impact to take them from 54/8 to 163. The last three batters played brilliantly to frustrate the hosts bowlers who bowled well with Noman Ali taking a hat trick and ending with a six fer. The trio then with the ball took all 10 wickets to take a lead of 9 runs. West Indies once again will be tested with the bat. The top order needs to step up this time. Can they though? Stay tuned to find out.
...DAY 2, SESSION 1...

Pakistan will be disappointed! They batted really poorly. A few of their batters got off to starts but none went on to make it into a decent score. They kept losing wickets and have ended up conceding a lead. However, they would know they would be eager to bowl the visitors out quite cheaply and would back themselves to do it on this wicket. Day two could turn out to be an exciting one and it won't come as a surprise if it is the last day too. Do join us for the coverage. Until then, goodbye and take care!
Roach was brilliant with the new ball and then it was all about Gudakesh Motie and Jomel Warrican. They two picked seven between them and have helped the visitors gain a small lead.

What a fine day of cricket! West Indies have fought back brilliantly! First it was the last wicket stand for them. They were reeling at 95 for 9 but the last wicket added more than 50 and gave their bowlers something to bowl at and they responded brilliantly.

OUT! RUN OUT! Ali is short! There is the end of the Pakistan innings. West Indies manage to gain a small lead. Sajid sweeps. It goes to short fine leg. Ali goes for the run. The throw is to the keeper who takes the bails off. Ali is well short.

Commentary.Commentary: We're back!
... DAY 1, SESSION 3 ...

Pakistan on the other hand, need a good partnership. They still trail by over 90 and they'll hope these two can bat for long. They would know any kind of lead on this surface could be handy. An interesting third session awaits.

West Indies have fought back well here! After being bowled out for a low score in the first session, their bowlers have responded well in the second. They have managed to take 4 wickets. Roach was brilliant with the new ball and Motie too weaved his magic. Warrican has looked threatening and Windies will hope they can get a few more quickly after the break.
